features.name: Entity Precedent Timeline
features.description: Searching a target name returns a chronological record of every prior touch the firm has had with that entity, its sponsors and its subsidiaries — which desk, which people, which meetings, which IC memos, which prior agreements — before any build work starts.
features.hmw: How might we make a firm's own prior contact with a target visible at the moment someone starts evaluating it, including the contact nobody remembers?

success_metric.name: Share of targets where prior firm contact is surfaced before manual hunting begins
success_metric.target: 80% of new assignments show precedent at orientation
success_metric.source: Instrumented at launch; no current system records this

features.name: Inbox and Drive Ingestion
features.description: Indexes the places firm memory actually lives — Outlook, SharePoint, shared and local drives, the credit document repository — into the precedent store, with the metadata tagging that keeps Private Equity notes invisible to Liquid Strategies unless permitted.
features.hmw: How might we make a firm's own prior contact with a target visible at the moment someone starts evaluating it, including the contact nobody remembers?

success_metric.name: Share of firm precedent reachable by search rather than by asking a colleague
success_metric.target: 90% of precedent sources indexed and searchable
success_metric.source: Index coverage report; no baseline exists because no search covers these stores today

features.name: Credit Agreement Term Extraction
features.description: Reads a credit agreement end to end and returns the figures that decide the credit: covenant definitions and thresholds, leverage ratios, the definition of EBITDA in this document, and the amortization schedule.
features.hmw: How might we shorten the distance between a term written into a credit agreement and a number an analyst can act on?

success_metric.name: Hours from receiving the agreement set to a committed term sheet
success_metric.baseline: Four to five hours of day one on the org chart alone
success_metric.target: Under one hour to committed terms

features.name: Auto-Built Org and Guarantee Chart
features.description: Derives the ultimate parent, co-issuers and guarantors from the agreement set and renders the corporate structure, marking which entities are on the hook for the debt and which subsidiaries are unrated or offshore.
features.hmw: How might we shorten the distance between a term written into a credit agreement and a number an analyst can act on?

success_metric.name: Hours to a verified corporate structure and guarantee package
success_metric.baseline: Four to five hours of day one on the org chart alone

features.name: Model Template Auto-Population
features.description: Extracted figures populate the profile model directly, so financials are never re-keyed from a PDF and the template's formulas are never manually repaired.
features.hmw: How might we shorten the distance between a term written into a credit agreement and a number an analyst can act on?

success_metric.name: Share of profile model fields re-keyed by hand from a PDF

features.name: Click-to-Source Provenance
features.description: Every figure in the profile links to the exact sentence in the document it came from, shown in place without leaving the profile or opening the underlying agreement.
features.hmw: How might we let a reviewer satisfy themselves that a figure is right without leaving the profile they are reading?

success_metric.name: Minutes per risk review spent reopening source documents to verify a figure
success_metric.baseline: Twenty to thirty minutes per review, verification by reopening the agreement

features.name: Add-Back and Pro-Forma Challenge Flags
features.description: Flags adjustments that warrant a question rather than acceptance: an EBITDA add-back described as one-time that recurs across periods, or a vendor pull not adjusted for a recent acquisition.
features.hmw: How might we let a reviewer satisfy themselves that a figure is right without leaving the profile they are reading?

success_metric.name: Share of questionable add-backs raised at review rather than after close
success_metric.target: Every recurring add-back described as one-time is flagged before sign-off

features.name: Outstanding-Input Tracker
features.description: The profile itself declares what it is waiting on, who owns the request, when it was made and how long it has been outstanding, so a blocked dependency is visible to everyone on the deal rather than sitting in one associate's inbox.
features.hmw: How might we keep the deal clock from being held hostage to a reply that has not arrived?

success_metric.name: Deal-clock days lost waiting on an unowned outstanding request
success_metric.target: No request goes unowned for more than one business day
success_metric.source: Outstanding-input ageing report once the tracker exists

features.name: In-Profile Review Threads
features.description: A reviewer returns a defect on the line item it concerns and the associate answers it there, so a correction never becomes a round of email and a minor fix is never absorbed silently to avoid one.
features.hmw: How might we keep the deal clock from being held hostage to a reply that has not arrived?

success_metric.name: Round trips to close a returned defect
success_metric.target: One round trip for the median defect

features.name: Continuous Position Health Score
features.description: Ingests daily alternative signals against each booked position and scores deviation from the sector benchmark, replacing the quarterly spreadsheet cycle with a standing measure.
features.hmw: How might we make a portfolio signal arrive early enough, and specific enough, to change what a Managing Director does that day?

success_metric.name: Lead time between a deterioration signal and it reaching the MD
success_metric.baseline: Roughly three months after the event

features.name: Decision-Carrying Alert Feed
features.description: A ranked feed where each entry carries the three things needed to act: what changed, the firm's direct exposure, and the current distance to the covenant threshold.
features.hmw: How might we make a portfolio signal arrive early enough, and specific enough, to change what a Managing Director does that day?

success_metric.name: Share of alerts acted on without opening another system to decide
success_metric.target: 80% of alerts actioned from the feed entry alone
success_metric.source: Alert acknowledge/escalate events with source of decision

design_directions.name: The Verifiable Profile
design_directions.summary: The product is the borrower profile itself, turned from a static deliverable into a live, interrogable document. Extraction fills it, provenance backs every figure, and review happens inside it. The associate stops transcribing and stops formatting for trust; the reviewer stops reopening agreements to check what she is reading.
design_directions.differentiator: Trust is the feature, not a by-product. Every other approach treats extraction as the goal and leaves the reviewer to believe the output; this one treats the reviewer's five-minute verification as the thing being built, and extraction exists to serve it.
hmws_addressed: How might we shorten the distance between a term written into a credit agreement and a number an analyst can act on?
How might we let a reviewer satisfy themselves that a figure is right without leaving the profile they are reading?
How might we keep the deal clock from being held hostage to a reply that has not arrived?
design_directions.tradeoff: Does nothing for the portfolio after the deal is booked. The Managing Director's three-months-too-late problem is untouched — and he is the one who described a line of users out the door. This direction wins the workflow and leaves the buying signal unaddressed.

design_directions.name: The Firm's Memory
design_directions.summary: The product is the cross-asset knowledge graph. The entry point is a target name and the payload is everything the firm already knows about it, drawn from CRM, repositories, drives and inboxes across every desk. Extraction and provenance are how the graph gets populated and trusted, not ends in themselves.
design_directions.differentiator: It is the only capability no incumbent has. Per the brief's own competitive read, DealCloud carries the CRM but cannot search unstructured internal content, and Preqin and PitchBook have no internal context at all. This is the one direction a competitor cannot answer by shipping a feature.
hmws_addressed: How might we make a firm's own prior contact with a target visible at the moment someone starts evaluating it, including the contact nobody remembers?
How might we shorten the distance between a term written into a credit agreement and a number an analyst can act on?
design_directions.tradeoff: Cold start. Value on day one is near zero and grows with corpus coverage and adoption, in a firm that expects immediate leverage — and the associate's 48-72 hour build barely moves until the graph is dense. It also carries the heaviest compliance surface: the RBAC wall between Private Equity and Liquid Strategies is load-bearing here, and getting it wrong is an insider-trading problem, not a bug.

design_directions.name: The Standing Watch
design_directions.summary: The product is continuous monitoring of booked positions. The pre-close profile is not the deliverable but the baseline: the covenant thresholds and exposure figures extracted at underwriting become the reference the daily signal is measured against, so screening work is retained rather than filed.
design_directions.differentiator: It is the only direction that closes the gap between a borrower's condition changing and the firm knowing, and the only one aimed squarely at the persona who controls the budget. It also reframes the profile build as an investment that keeps paying rather than a document that is archived.
hmws_addressed: How might we make a portfolio signal arrive early enough, and specific enough, to change what a Managing Director does that day?
How might we let a reviewer satisfy themselves that a figure is right without leaving the profile they are reading?
design_directions.tradeoff: It bets on the thinnest evidence in the corpus. Post-close monitoring was raised by one participant of three, while the associate's build and the reviewer's rework — five consecutive high-drop-off journey stages — are largely out of scope. It is also the highest technical risk: the alternative-data signals it depends on were named by the product team, not by any user, and no participant was ever asked what false-positive rate they would tolerate.
